blocks: That local number calling you? It might not be local at all.
In just three months, one operation made ninety-six million robocalls. The FCC says the callers faked their numbers, so they looked like they came from your own neighborhood.
The trick is called neighbor spoofing. The fake number copies the first six digits of your own.
Press one, and you reach a call center selling vacation packages, using names like TripAdvisor, Expedia, Marriott and Hilton. Those companies never made the calls.
And here is the twist. The real owners of those faked numbers started getting angry calls back, from strangers, over calls they never made.
So remember. A local number on your screen proves nothing. Do not press one. Do not call back. Hang up.
The full case, the record fine, and the law it changed, is on The Rule Changed.
